methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $30M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 1 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 21.5x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

private.name: SambaNova Systems
private.rationale: Same sector (Chips & Semiconductors), same stage (Series A), post-money $11B

data.narrative:
Looking Glass, a Series A semiconductor company founded by Shawn Frayne, has raised $30M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a universe of 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, including SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, and Etched.

Of the three valuation methods assessed, only Stage-Progression proved applicable. This method applies a standard 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage transitions, using the $30M total raised as a proxy baseline. This yields an implied valuation of $60M. Peer-Median analysis was not executable due to insufficient narrow-set comparables—while the sector contains 12 same-stage and adjacent-stage peers, fewer than three met tight similarity criteria. Public-Comp Anchoring could not be applied because Looking Glass does not disclose revenue, preventing meaningful deployment of the 21.5x P/S median observed across public semiconductor peers.

The triangulation analysis, constrained to a single applicable method, supports a valuation range of $51M (low) to $69M (high), centered on $60M. This relatively tight $18M band reflects the methodology's internal consistency rather than cross-method validation. Key uncertainties include: the absence of comparable transaction data for same-stage semiconductor players; undisclosed revenue that would anchor multiples-based approaches; and stage-specific market conditions for frontier hardware companies. Additional data on Looking Glass's revenue run-rate or customer traction would substantially narrow this range.
